most_important_fix: Close the history-distribution (transport) gap in Theorem 6, which is advertised as Route D's central new contribution and is currently not a usable bound. The performance-difference identity is stated with the outer expectation over P^U, the REAL user's history distribution, while every quantity the harness can compute — span(q_bar_t(h,·)), rho_t, Q_t^{Uhat}(h,·) — is only estimable at histories the SIMULATOR reaches, and rho_t^U additionally requires evaluating Q at the real user's own messages at real-user histories, i.e. branching from human logs, which §10.2 declares impossible. So Corollary 6.2's "two separately estimable numbers, one from logs and one from the oracle" is false as written: the first term needs S_#U_t(·|h) (from logs, fine) multiplied by span(q_bar_t(h,·)) at those same log histories (not obtainable), integrated over P^U (not obtainable). Fix: (a) restate the PDL in the roll-in-under-Uhat form and carry an explicit, named third term for the history shift — either a bounded density ratio / chi-square divergence between the S-coarsened history laws, or an explicitly-labelled untestable transport assumption with its own number; (b) define rho_t^U on a reachable, pre-registered set of replayed human prefixes and state exactly what resettability of those prefixes requires (same frozen receiver, same decoding config, A2/A3 verified by Proposition 13(i)) — or admit rho_t^U is not estimable and give a crude sup bound instead; (c) demote the "two estimable numbers" claim to "one estimable number plus one bounded-by-design term plus one transport term we cannot estimate", since as stated it repeats exactly the kind of overclaim §12 warns against. While doing this, also write out the assumption list: A6, A7, A10, A11, A12, A13, A14, A15 are cited by name in theorem statements but never stated anywhere, so Theorems 2, 4, 8 and Proposition 13 cannot actually be checked against their hypotheses (A13 never appears at all).
errors: Theorem 6 / Corollary 6.2 — distribution mismatch (the main mathematical gap). The identity's outer expectation is over P^U (real-user history law); all of span(q_bar_t), Q_t^{Uhat}(h,·) and rho_t are estimable only on the simulator/branch history law. No result in the document bridges the two, so the inequality has no estimable right-hand side and the advertised 'two separately estimable numbers' conclusion does not follow. rho_t^U in particular requires executing the REAL user's messages at REAL-user histories, i.e. branching human logs, which §10 item 2 declares impossible — an internal contradiction.

Theorem 8(3) — the bound |CDE − NDE| <= kappa·Lip is structurally wrong, not merely loose-constant. CDE at leakage 0 and the NDE differ by (i) the sanitizer's style displacement AND (ii) the difference between setting the mediator to 0 and to its natural level under a_ref, i.e. the style×leakage interaction. Term (ii) is not bounded by kappa (style displacement) under any Lipschitz-in-style condition; it is exactly the quantity that makes CDE != NDE even when kappa = 0. As written the inequality is false, not open.

Theorem 8(1) — 'controlled direct effect at leakage level 0' is not well defined without a factorization assumption. CDE language presupposes that a decomposes into an independently manipulable (style, content) pair, i.e. that a message with prescribed S-value and prescribed leakage level is constructible. The route needs this as a numbered assumption; otherwise E[Y|do(R(a))] − E[Y|do(R(a'))] is the effect of sanitized messages (a perfectly fine estimand) but not a CDE of anything.

Proposition 12(2) — L1/L2 conflation. rho_t = E|Q − q_bar| is NOT 'equivalently' the within-cell variance Var_{a|S(a)=s}(Q). One has only rho <= sqrt(E[r^2]) by Cauchy–Schwarz, and equality of E[r]=0 requires q_bar to be defined as the within-cell MEAN of Q under the chosen within-cell candidate law — which Corollary 6.2's decomposition never specifies. The ANOVA estimator therefore estimates a quantity that upper-bounds, but does not equal, the rho entering Corollary 6.2.

Proposition 12(1) — permutation test exactness. H_0 as stated is a null on conditional MEANS. A within-cell permutation test of candidate labels is exact only under the SHARP null of equal conditional outcome DISTRIBUTIONS within the cell; with candidate-dependent outcome variances (very plausible: a vague message yields higher-variance outputs than a precise one) the test is not exact and can reject at well above nominal level. Either sharpen H_0 or use a studentized/asymptotic within-cell test.

Proposition 11 — the constant 2 does not follow from the proof given. For a binary one-step deviation the loss at h is |gamma(h)|, and on the sign-error event |gamma(h)| <= |gamma_hat − gamma|, so the bound is E[|gamma_hat − gamma| 1{error}], with no factor 2. The 2 is correct only for the >2-action Q-function argument (|Q_hat−Q|(a*) + |Q_hat−Q|(a_hat)). Also 'V(pi*) − V(pi_hat) <= 2E|gamma_hat − gamma| on the sign-error event' is malformed: the event restriction belongs inside the expectation.

Proposition 3 — bound presented as value. sigma*sqrt(2 log K / n_b) is an upper bound on E[max_k e_k]; for K=8 iid Gaussian errors the actual expected maximum is about 1.43 sigma, not 2.04 sigma. The headline 'at K=8, n_b=1 the inflation is ≈ 2 sigma' overstates the artifact by ~40%. Say 'at most ≈2 sigma' (and note the sub-Gaussian proxy assumption, which for bounded Y at n_b=1 is not sigma).

Proposition 1 — 'positivity ... min_a q_t(a|H_t) >= 1/K' is false for non-uniform designs. With a floored but non-uniform randomization the floor is whatever delta the design enforces, which can be arbitrarily below 1/K. State the floor as delta and carry delta, not 1/K, through §4 and the Route C handshake.

Theorem 4(c)(ii) — the inference-time cost claim is wrong as phrased. Greedy execution with ROLLOUTS UNDER A FIXED CONTINUATION POLICY costs O(K·(T−t)) receiver calls per decision, not K^{T−t}. K^{T−t} is the cost of exhaustive recursive tree search over history-dependent continuations. As written the statement conflates the two and inflates the case for a learned critic (which is still easily made at O(K(T−t)) per turn).

A1 vs Theorem 9 — foundational inconsistency. A1 posits a single exogenous xi generating Y(a) for ALL a, which by construction defines a joint law of potential outcomes across arms (hence well-defined within-unit win probabilities and individual-effect variances). Theorem 9(3)-(4) then argues the coupling is implementation-defined and has 'no real-world referent'. Both cannot be the foundational reading. If only marginals are meaningful, potential outcomes should be defined as arm-specific DISTRIBUTIONS (stochastic-intervention / do-on-a-randomized-mechanism semantics) rather than via a shared xi; T9(2) then becomes 'not identified' rather than 'not meaningful', which are different claims and the text slides between them.

Theorem 9(2) — misattribution of Finkelstein–Schoenfeld. The standard FS / win-ratio estimand compares pairs formed ACROSS independent units in different arms; it is a functional of the arm marginals and IS identified by branching. Only a within-unit (paired-counterfactual) version depends on the coupling. Listing 'within-unit prioritized (Finkelstein–Schoenfeld) comparisons' as the canonical FS object mislabels the classical estimand, even though §8's closing remark gets the between/within distinction right.

Corollary 6.1 — 'two distinct text-generating policies have near-disjoint supports' is technically false for softmax LLM policies, which put positive probability on every finite string, so the supports are identical. What is true is near-mutual-singularity of the high-probability mass, giving TV ≈ 1 up to exponentially small overlap. The conclusion survives; the stated reason does not.

Proposition 7(2) vs 7(4) — the interval is anti-conservative if the audit is used to supply delta. 7(2) uses A8's delta = a bound on TOTAL differential judge bias; 7(4) estimates only style sensitivity on the manipulated dimensions at fixed programmatic content signature, which is a lower bound on that total. The document notes the asymmetry in prose but still chains 7(4) into 7(2) operationally. Also 'gamma* in [gamma_hat ± delta]' holds only for the n_b -> infinity limit of gamma_hat; the finite-sample statement must widen a confidence interval by delta, not a point estimate.

Theorem 10 — estimand mismatch not flagged. gamma_tilde from branch contrasts is unbiased for the blip under the BRANCH continuation regime; gamma_hat may be fit to target the blip under a reference or optimal continuation. Unless the continuations coincide, the 'debiased validation risk' is unbiased for the risk against the wrong target. P11 flags the continuation ambiguity as OPEN but T10 silently assumes it away.

Theorem 2(iv) / §11 Route B handshake — scope error. An LMTP or incremental-propensity intervention is DEFINED relative to a base user kernel. What the harness executes is the tilt of Uhat, so it identifies the value of an MTP on the simulator's kernel, not on U. Route B's estimands are defined relative to the observational (real) kernel, so 'Route D provides ground truth for Route B's estimators' is valid only when Route B's estimator is run on harness-generated behaviour data with the harness's own base kernel. Stated without that restriction, it is false.

Proposition 5 — cost model omits the prefix cost. B ∝ n·n_b ignores that each new history costs a roll-in of length t to reach. With B ∝ n(c_0 + n_b) the monotonicity conclusion survives, but the stated proportionality is not the actual budget constraint and the 'strictly increasing in n_b' claim also needs sigma_m^2 > 0 (it is flat in n_b under a correctly specified blip model). Also B and B' are used interchangeably in the displayed formula.

Presentation defect with rigor consequences: A6, A7, A10, A11, A12, A14, A15 are invoked in the hypotheses of Theorems 2, 4, 8 and Propositions 12, 14 but never stated; A13 never appears at all. §1 promises 'assumptions A1–A15' and delivers roughly A1–A5 plus A9 inline. The correctness of T2 and T4 cannot be verified as stated.

Proposition 13(i) — 'near-certain power' is asserted without any power argument, and under the document's own A1/zeta nondeterminism the next-token log-probability vector is not exactly reproducible, so the test is a distributional two-sample test on a high-dimensional statistic with unstated multiplicity control. Downgrade to 'high power against version drift and prefix mismatch, power against subtle state leakage OPEN'.
keep_these_ideas: Theorem 4 as the answer to 'why do you need causal inference if you have an oracle': positivity is not eliminated but converted into a purchased budget, with an information-theoretic Omega(K^T) barrier that only structure can break. This is the correct and most defensible framing of the whole route and should open the paper.

Theorem 10 (debiased validation risk with the MC-noise offset subtracted, and the observation that the offset cancels for estimator RANKINGS so no variance estimate is needed to compare). Real unbiased conditional-effect labels on a real system is genuinely something applied causal inference does not have; make this the headline experiment.

Proposition 12: branching makes Route A's treatment-coarsening sufficiency falsifiable at a fixed history, plus the caveat that rho is only as honest as the pre-registered within-cell candidate diversity. The caveat is as valuable as the test.

Proposition 5's design dichotomy: wide-shallow (n_b = 1 paired contrast, maximal history coverage) for fitting blips versus narrow-deep (n_b >= 8) for pointwise oracle truth and for estimating the v(h) that Theorem 10 needs. Concrete, cheap, immediately actionable.

Theorem 9's warning that shared seeds manufacture a joint that has no real-world referent, together with the prescription to couple only genuinely exogenous inputs (task instance, replayed tool responses, evaluator seed) as common random numbers. The between-unit vs within-unit win-probability distinction should be stated as a hard constraint on Route E.

Proposition 7(4): the judge is itself a resettable frozen model, so its differential bias becomes the estimand of an auxiliary branching experiment with programmatically enforced content fixity — plus the honest admission that this is unavailable exactly where judges are most needed.

Theorem 8's reframing of information leakage as a design problem (executable graded redaction series, headline effects reported as effects at leakage level 0, per-class answer-transfer probe) rather than an identification problem.

Proposition 13's four falsification tests (resume fidelity on log-prob vectors, duplicate arms, randomized execution order, snapshot-hash assertion) and the norm that a run not reporting them is not an experiment. This should be a checklist in the paper's methods section.

Proposition 14: replay continuation identifies a static regime with a stale-reference pathology whose bias is plausibly adverse to beneficial interventions, so it is usable only as a conservative anchor or for immediately-measured outcomes. No medical analogue; worth its own subsection.
Proposition 3's point that 'branch eight prompts and report the best' is an artifact, with cross-fitted selection/evaluation splitting as the remedy.

most_important_fix: Reconcile Theorem 5 with Theorem 2. As stated they contradict each other: A3 is assumed at the FINE level, L is countable, and a* is required to lie in the observed support, so delta_{a*} << p(.|h) and Theorem 2 already POINT-IDENTIFIES psi(d*). The sharpness proof ("the observed law constrains only the p-average of Q on each slice, not its shape") is therefore false — Q_t^{d0}(h,a) = E[V_{t+1}|H_t=h, A_t=a] is a functional of the observed law at every a with p(a|h)>0. Two admissible repairs, and the document must pick one explicitly: (i) state Theorem 5 relative to a COARSENED observed-data law in which A_t is not recorded, only (H_t,S_t,O_t) — but then Proposition 10's refinement tests and Proposition 13's Lambda coordinate, which both read the message text, are unavailable, so this is a real cost; or (ii) keep the fine data and restate the result as "psi(d*) is identified but not regularly estimable — any estimator has effective sample size n * p(a*|h) = n * e^{-Theta(m)}", with the Tρ interval reinterpreted as a finite-sample/irregularity band rather than an identified set. Option (ii) is the honest one and it strengthens the paper's own thesis (the obstruction is estimability, not identification), but it requires rewriting verdict items 2–3, Theorem 2's "support inclusion rather than bounded positivity" gloss, and Theorem 5's sharpness clause. While fixing this, correct the breakdown value: under A12 the reference continuation is a singleton (version-free) class, so a turn-t blip has exactly ONE version-ambiguous turn, and the breakdown defect is rho* = |gamma_hat| (per-turn, standardized), not |gamma_hat|/T.
errors: THEOREM 5 vs THEOREM 2 (fatal, internal contradiction). Under fine-level A3, countable L, and a* in the observed support, delta_{a*} << p so Theorem 2 identifies psi(d*) exactly. Theorem 5's sharpness argument ('the observed law constrains only the p-average of Q on each slice, not its shape') is false: for every a with p(a|h)>0, Q_t^{d0}(h,a)=E[V_{t+1}|H_t=h,A_t=a] is a functional of the observed law. The partial-identification claim is valid only w.r.t. a coarsened observed-data law in which A_t is unrecorded — which the rest of the document contradicts (Prop 10 refines on message features W; Prop 13 computes Lambda from the message). Correct statement: identified but irregularly estimable at rate e^{-Theta(m)}.

BREAKDOWN VALUE OFF BY A FACTOR OF T. rho* = |gamma_hat|/T is inconsistent with A12. Theorem 5's bound is Sum_{t=1}^T E^{d*}[D_t]; a turn-t blip gamma_t deviates from the reference at ONE turn and the reference continuation is a singleton class, hence version-free, so all other terms vanish. The breakdown defect for a blip is rho* = |gamma_hat| (one term), not |gamma_hat|/T. As written the reported sensitivity is T-fold too conservative — and the text presents it as the headline sensitivity number.

PROPOSITION 7 MONOTONICITY IS FALSE FOR THE L2 DEFECT. 'refining S weakly decreases D pointwise (each refined slice is a subset)' holds for the range D but NOT for sigma, which is the only version Proposition 9 can estimate. Counterexample: a parent slice with Q-values {0,0.5,1} at probabilities (0.98,0.01,0.01) has Var = 0.0123; the refined sub-slice {0.5,1} at 50/50 has Var = 0.0625 > parent. Only the p-weighted AVERAGE of sub-slice variances decreases (law of total variance). Since the bias-variance tradeoff of Prop 7 and the taxonomy-design rule both rest on this monotonicity, the claim must be restated as monotone-on-average for sigma, pointwise only for D.

PROPOSITION 13, THIRD CLAUSE: PROOF INVALID. 'refinement monotonicity (Proposition 7) gives D(proxy) >= D(ideal)' does not follow, because a proxy leakage functional Lambda_hat does not induce a refinement of the ideal Lambda-binning — neither sigma-algebra contains the other. Nothing bounds the direction: within a Lambda_hat bin, true leakage can still be correlated with the severity/specificity class, so the identified within-bin contrast can be LARGER in absolute value than the ideal leakage-fixed contrast. The honest statement is that the within-Lambda_hat contrast is a valid causal contrast for a different coarsening, whose relation to the leakage-fixed contrast is unsigned. This matters because leakage control is advertised as Route A's cleanest win.

PROPOSITION 8 CONFLATES IPW VARIANCE WITH THE EFFICIENCY BOUND, AND MISSTATES THE MOMENT. (a) E[W^2 Y^2] = K^T E^d[Y^2] (the ON-REGIME second moment), not K^T E[Y^2] under the observational law; as written the bound is evaluated at the wrong measure. (b) The semiparametric efficiency bound is Var(V_1(H_1)) + Sum_t E[(prod_{k<=t} 1{S_k=pi}/g_k^2) Var(V_{t+1}|H_t,S_t)], i.e. K^t weights multiply per-step RESIDUAL variances, not E[Y^2]. So consequence 3 ('DR helps the constant, not the exponent') is right about the exponent but understates the constant: if Var(Y|H_T,S_T) is well below 0.25 the requirement can be several-fold smaller than 3.5e5 episodes. The design conclusions K<=5 and delta>=0.2 should be re-derived from the efficient bound, not from unaugmented IPW, or explicitly labelled as worst-case.

THEOREM 4 IS VACUOUS IN THE CASE THAT MOTIVATES IT (A6b). For a pinned generator G versus a human within-class writing mix p, chi^2(G || p) is of order e^{Theta(message length)}, so the bound sqrt(chi^2) * sigma exceeds 1 and says nothing. Relatedly, the verdict's headline ('the hopeless e^{-Theta(m)} probabilities never appear') holds ONLY under A6a: in Theorem 3's proof the fine densities cancel because q = p(.|s,h); under A6b they do not cancel, so a generator regime is NOT off-policy estimable from human logs and must be rolled out. This scope restriction should be stated where the headline claim is made, not left to be inferred from Sec 7 item 4.

PROPOSITION 9 ESTIMATES THE DEFECT OF A DIFFERENT ESTIMAND. tau^2 is the dispersion under the mix you can SAMPLE, while sigma_t in Sec 5 and D_t in Theorem 5 are defined under the logged human mix p(.|s,h). Branching requires (i) sampling versions from p(.|s,h) and (ii) rolling out the reference continuation d0 = (pi,p) — both need a model of the human intervener's within-class writing behaviour. With an LLM version-writer and an LLM continuation, tau_hat^2 estimates dispersion of Q^{d0'} under a generator mix, which neither bounds nor is bounded by sigma_p. Either add the assumption that the version-writer reproduces p(.|s,h) (and say it is strong), or redefine the estimand's version mix to be the generator's from the start — which also makes A6b, not A6a, the operative case and reopens the previous item.

THEOREM 2's 'support inclusion rather than bounded positivity' needs the estimability qualifier. Well-definedness of the functional needs only q << p, but the functional conditions on events of probability e^{-Theta(m)} and admits no regular estimator; stating 'identified' unqualified in verdict item 2 reproduces the confusion that Theorem 5 then trips over.

THEOREM 6 SUP RANGES AND POLICY CLASS UNDER-SPECIFIED. D^+_t uses sup_a with no stated range; if the sup runs over all of L then V(fine*) is not identified and the bound compares an identified quantity to an unidentified one. fine* must be restricted to support-inclusion regimes and both sups to the p-support (Sec 5 says this for D but not for D^+). Also the sup need not be attained in countable L — an epsilon-argument is required (trivial, but the proof asserts an attaining a^+).

THEOREM 3, SECOND CLAIM, IS TRUE ONLY WITH VERBATIM HISTORIES AS STATES. 'the coarsened process (H_t,S_t,O_t) is itself a valid longitudinal causal model' holds when H_t is the full verbatim history. If H_t is read as the coarse history (X,S_1,O_1,...), the kernel p(O_t|H_t,S_t) = int M(O_t|H_t,a) P(da|S_t,H_t) is not the stated mixture unless the within-class mix depends on the past only through the coarse history — an A9-type condition that is never invoked here. Readers will take the stronger reading; say which is meant.

PROPOSITION 12's JUSTIFICATION IS NOT AN ARGUMENT. 'a product of independently attenuated factors is not an attenuated product' does not establish non-attenuation; in the classical nondifferential case per-turn attenuation composes to an attenuated product. The conclusion (no guaranteed direction for longitudinal misclassification in the WEIGHTS, where errors enter the denominators and are non-monotone) is likely right but needs either a worked two-turn counterexample or downgrading to a flagged OPEN.

THE OFF-SUPPORT CAVEAT IS ATTACHED TO THEOREM 5 ONLY, BUT APPLIES EQUALLY TO THEOREM 4. Theorem 4's bound is E^d[...] over histories reachable under d, which may lie outside the logged support; sigma_t must then be assumed (not estimated) there. State the caveat once, for Theorems 4, 5 and 6 together.

PROPOSITION 15: 'precision capped by |V|' is imprecise and the estimator is under-specified. The asymptotic variance is Var(phi(Y_J))/n + Var(w e)/|V|; the cap binds only when the influence-weighted judge error has non-negligible variance (that is exactly the PPI gain). Also unbiasedness of the rectifier requires w_i to be the influence-function weights evaluated at the SAME nuisances used in gamma_hat(Y_J), with cross-fitting so that w_i is independent of the validation draw — neither is stated.
keep_these_ideas: The diagnosis that do(S_t = s) is ILL-POSED rather than merely unidentified (Prop 1), and that in a language action space this is generic. Making the version distribution q part of the estimand (a Robins random dynamic strategy) is the right repair and should be the framing for the whole project, not just Route A.

The exact weight collapse of Theorem 3 as the precise statement of what coarsening buys: the fine ratio cancels identically under the natural mix, delta^{-1} replaces e^{Theta(m)} — together with the explicitly named price, that the coarse blip is a property of (receiver, task distribution, INTERVENER POPULATION). This honesty about estimand inheritance is the document's best single paragraph.

The graded exclusion restriction E1 => E2 => E3 with the observation that only E3 is ever used, plus the three plausibility mechanisms (coarse/binary outcome absorbs kernel differences; an adaptive continuation repairs version noise, so exclusion is more plausible early and least plausible at the last turn; the class already pins outcome-relevant content). The per-turn prediction is genuinely testable and should be pre-registered.

One dispersion functional with three faces (Prop 7): exclusion validity, version-mix transportability, abstraction loss — and the result that the bias is ADDITIVE in T rather than compounding (performance-difference telescoping). Keep this as the organizing device even after the monotonicity claim is corrected.

Branching as a way to report a causal assumption WITH A CONFIDENCE INTERVAL (Prop 9, one-way random-effects ANOVA), together with the negative half: the sup-form defect is not estimable from finitely many sampled versions. And the methodological instruction 'test nothing; estimate' — H0: sigma = 0 is a priori false, so report sigma_hat plus a breakdown value.

Leakage as a PRE-TREATMENT coordinate of S rather than a mediator (Prop 13's framing, not its third clause), with the placebo-solver / reference-log-likelihood-gain operationalization of Lambda, stratified randomization on the bin, and the verification that within a bin message length no longer predicts Y.

Prop 11 and Prop 12 as numbered warnings: post-treatment labelling ('was this feedback helpful?') is selection on the outcome and gives a contrast of 1 even for a receiver that ignores A_t; a stochastic labeler is misclassification, not coarsening, and pinning it converts a bias problem into a measurable design choice.

The positivity budget as a hard design constraint (K^T scaling; small K; per-turn-overlap g-estimation of a coarse SNMM as the PRIMARY estimand; direct rollout for regime values when the environment is resettable). Even after re-deriving the constants from the efficiency bound, the qualitative conclusions and the willingness to state 'do not report an off-policy interval three times the effect size' should survive.

Prop 14's asymmetry: coarsening the ACTION is innocuous for identification because the target integrates over versions, whereas coarsening the HISTORY is innocuous only under A9 — true by construction in a micro-randomized design, essentially never in human logs. This is the cleanest argument in the document for why the confirmatory arm must be randomized.

Singleton references (STOP, and an exact fixed retry string) with the two-way decomposition they license — 'is another turn worth taking' versus 'does the content matter holding the retry fixed' — and the rule against non-singleton references such as 'generic mild feedback'.

Judge outcomes inside a PPI wrapper with arm-by-arm validation, plus the setting-specific sting that in Route A judge bias is correlated with treatment BY DESIGN because the taxonomy axes (severity, tone, concision) are exactly the axes that move judge-perceived quality.

Sec 13's two implementation payoffs: nuisance regressions condition on the CLASS, never on the message, so no generative text model is needed anywhere; and the flag that the product-rate condition licensing root-n inference is unverifiable for text-valued histories.

errors: FALSE HEADLINE IDENTITY (T4). The boxed claim E_P[R_T^2] = E_P[prod_t (1+chi^2_t(H_t))] is wrong. Correct algebra: w_t^2 = (1+chi^2_t(H_t)) * w_t^{(2theta)} where w^{(2theta)} is the tilt weight at parameter 2theta (conditional mean one). Hence R_T^2 = prod_t(1+chi^2_t(H_t)) * dP^{q^{2theta}}/dP and therefore E_P[R_T^2] = E_{P^{q^{2theta}}}[prod_t (1+chi^2_t(H_t))] -- the expectation is under the DOUBLY TILTED law, not under P. The proof in the paper silently treats chi^2_{t+1}(H_{t+1}) as independent of w_t: the induction step E[R_{T-1}^2(1+chi^2_T(H_T))] cannot be factored because Cov(w_{T-1}^2, chi^2_T(H_T) | H_{T-1}) is generally nonzero (tilting toward high specificity moves you into histories with different conditional feature variance). The exact object is the backward recursion Gamma_{T+1}=1, Gamma_t(h)=E[w_t^2 Gamma_{t+1}(H_{t+1}) | H_t=h], E[R_T^2]=E[Gamma_1]. Consequences: T4(i)'s sup bound survives (it is measure-free); T4(ii) survives only to O(theta^2) (the measure change contributes O(theta^3)); T4(iii)'s claim that 'the identity is exact and clean' under conditional Gaussianity is FALSE unless sigma_t^2 is nonrandom (homoskedastic across histories). Since T4 is the route's flagship 'computable in advance' result, this needs repair, and KL_tot must be defined under the correct measure.

ARITHMETIC INCONSISTENCY in the KL budget numbers. The boxed rule is KL_tot <= (1/2)log(n/n_eff^min), but Section 0 item 4 states '(1/2) log n' and both numerical examples use log n, i.e. n_eff^min = 1 (an effective sample size of one). With n=10^4, T=5, n_eff^min=100: sum_t Delta_t^2 <= log(100)=4.61, so Delta_t <= 0.96 SD per turn, not the 1.36 SD claimed in T4(iii), and KL_t <= 0.46 nats, not 0.9. Every headline number about how far one can extrapolate from logs is a factor of two too generous in KL and ~1.4x too generous in SD.

THE BUDGET IS DERIVED FROM THE WRONG VARIANCE. T4 computes E[R_T^2], the second moment of the sequential IPW weight, and then treats n_eff = n/E[R_T^2] as governing 'any importance-weighted estimator' and the whole analysis. But the recommended estimator E3 is efficient with variance Var(D_P) = Var(tildeQ_1) + sum_t E[R_t^2 (tildeQ_{t+1}-tildeQ_t)^2], which involves R_t^2 multiplied by tilted Bellman residuals and can be orders of magnitude smaller than E[R_T^2] when residuals are small. So the 'statistically certifiable KL radius' is an IPW-based, not an efficiency-bound-based, quantity; as stated it understates what is learnable from n logs. The honest version is a bound on Var(D_P) (e.g. via Cauchy-Schwarz with residual sup-norms), or an explicit statement that the budget is the worst case over outcome models.

P6 ('T2-T5 apply verbatim') IS NOT JUSTIFIED and is very likely false. The leakage-neutral tilt has a multiplier theta_2 = theta_2(h) defined implicitly by the moment equation partial_{theta_2} kappa_t(theta,h) = E_g[phi^leak | h]. This is a second, history-indexed, P-DEPENDENT nuisance. T2's derivative calculation assumed P-dependence enters only through Z_t, so differentiating along a path now produces an extra term of the form E[R_{t-1} tildeQ_t(H_t) * (d theta_2/d eps)(H_t) * (phi^leak - E_g[phi^leak|H_t]) * s], which does not vanish (R_T Y correlates with phi^leak within history strata). The EIF therefore has an additional component and the EXACT double robustness of T3(i) almost certainly fails, because perturbing theta_2 does not enter as a pure multiplicative H_t-measurable factor the way Z_t/barZ_t does. P6 needs its own EIF derivation or must be downgraded to 'identified, efficiency theory open'.

T1's WEIGHTED REPRESENTATION IS WRONG FOR NATURAL-VALUE-DEPENDENT REGIMES. T1 says 'q may depend on the natural value A_t' and then writes R_T = prod_t q_t(A_t|H_t)/g_t(A_t|H_t). For a natural-value-dependent kernel q_t(a'|h_t,a_t) the correct density ratio uses the INDUCED marginal kernel tildeq_t(a'|h_t) = sum_a g_t(a|h_t) q_t(a'|h_t,a) (Diaz et al.'s weights involve preimages under the shift map, not q/g). The same inconsistency appears in the definition tildeQ_t(h)=E_{a~q_t(.|h)}[Q_t(h,a)], which already presumes no natural-value dependence. Fix by stating T1 only for kernels q_t(.|h_t), which is all the tilt family needs, and removing the 'possibly depending on the natural value' clause (or handling it properly).

P4 CONFLATES TWO FAMILIES and the audit degrades exactly where it is needed. Softmax-of-K selection with weight e^{theta phi} converges to q^theta as K -> infinity with theta fixed; best-of-K by phi is the theta -> infinity limit at FIXED K, which is not q^theta for any theta and whose TV error bound O(chi^2_t/K) diverges as theta grows. So the claimed 'continuous interpolation from the natural user (theta=0) to best-of-K (theta=infinity)' is not a single family, and the randomized calibration arm -- advertised as the only direct audit of A3 -- is only a valid audit of Psi(theta) for small theta/large K. Separately, best-of-K has a bounded density ratio (<= K) and is arguably the better runnable estimand; it deserves its own analysis rather than being presented as a tilt limit.

P4's SAMPLING PREMISE IS NOT SATISFIABLE BY THE STATED PROTOCOLS. (i) requires K i.i.d. draws from g_t(.|h_t). Asking a real user for K drafts yields correlated, order-dependent, anchored drafts, and 'presenting K paraphrases of the user's own message' is a NATURAL-VALUE-DEPENDENT regime (it conditions on the realized A_t) with a different estimand and a different weight (see the T1 error above). Only a resettable user simulator actually delivers i.i.d. draws, which quietly makes the whole route's validation arm contingent on Route C.

T5(iv) AGGREGATES ACROSS TURNS INCORRECTLY and contradicts P9. Per-turn gain is sigma_t * sqrt(2 KL_t) (T5(iii)); maximizing sum_t sigma_t sqrt(2 eps_t) subject to sum_t eps_t = eps gives sqrt(2 eps * sum_t sigma_t^2) by Cauchy-Schwarz, i.e. a factor sqrt(T) larger than the stated 'sd(Q*) sqrt(2 eps)' when the sigma_t are comparable. P9 does the aggregation correctly (sqrt(eps b' barV^{-1} b) with b and barV summed over t), so the two results disagree. Also, Q*_t already internalizes future tilting, so 'per-turn gains' are not additive in the naive sense.

P9 USES A FIRST-ORDER EXPANSION AT A RADIUS WHERE IT IS INVALID. b = grad V(0) is a local (theta -> 0) object, yet the recommended radius is eps ~ log(n/n_eff^min) ~ 4.6, i.e. an aggregate shift of about 2 within-history SDs -- far outside the regime where V(theta) ~ b'theta. Psi(theta) is not concave in theta in general and is bounded in [0,1] by A8, so 'predicted gain = sqrt(eps b' barV^{-1} b)' can exceed the maximum possible gain of 1. This must be stated as a local diagnostic, or replaced by direct evaluation of Psi(theta) on a grid with the T4 diagnostics reported at each theta.

P7's CLIPPING PROPOSAL VIOLATES A6. 'Clipping at conditional quantiles' makes phi a functional of P (conditional quantiles of phi given H_t are unknown nuisances), so it is not a frozen, pre-specified feature map; the estimand becomes data-adaptive and its EIF acquires terms from estimating the clipping thresholds, which T2/T3 do not cover. Rank-normalizing within stratum has the same problem. Only unconditional, pre-specified bounded transforms of phi actually satisfy P7's own proof. Also, the sentence 'weight stabilization in Route B does not introduce the usual unquantified IPW bias' is true only for phi-transforms; per-turn clipping of the weights w_t themselves -- which is what the cited Route C toolkit means -- does bias, and the text invites that conflation.

A10's RATE CONDITION IS INSUFFICIENT FOR T>1. The remainder in T3(ii) is sum_t E[(barR_{t-1} Z_t/barZ_t - R_{t-1}) eps_t], and barR_{t-1} - R_{t-1} = O(sum_{s<t} ||barZ_s - Z_s||). So the remainder contains CROSS terms ||hatZ_s - Z_s|| * ||eps_t|| for s < t, which the stated condition (which pairs index t with index t) does not control. The correct sufficient condition is something like (max_s ||hatZ_s - Z_s||) * (sum_t ||eps_t||) = o_P(n^{-1/2}), or a per-pair product condition over all s <= t.

L1(c) MISWRITES THE VARIANCE LOWER BOUND. As written, E[prod_t 1{A_t=a_t}/g_t(a_t|H_t)]^2 is the SQUARE OF A MEAN, and that mean equals 1 exactly (the indicator weight has conditional mean one), so the displayed quantity is 1, not >= delta^{-2T}. The intended object is the second moment E[(prod_t 1{A_t=a_t}/g_t)^2] >= delta^{-T} (and >= delta^{-2T} only when the numerator is also tracked correctly). Same paragraph: delta_a := min_h g_t(a|h) = e^{-Theta(len(a))} is stated unconditionally but is 0 for the human-user case that L1(d) immediately describes.

T5(ii) OVERSELLS 'NO OFF-SUPPORT EXTRAPOLATION'. The soft-optimal recursion needs tildeQ*_t(h) = tau log E_g[e^{Q*_t(h,A)/tau} | H_t=h], i.e. the conditional MGF of the CRITIC over the messages the user might have sent at h. From observational logs each history is seen once with one action, so this requires a text-conditioned critic Q*_t(h,a) evaluated at (h,a) pairs never observed -- on-support in the measure-theoretic sense, but still an extrapolation of a text-to-text regression to unobserved action-history pairs. The practical gap between T5 and the generator-replacement case that P5 declares 'not estimable' is therefore much narrower than the table in 11.5 suggests; the honest distinction is 'extrapolation within supp(g)' vs 'extrapolation outside supp(g)', not 'no extrapolation' vs 'extrapolation'.

T5's KL CONSTRAINT IS MEASURE-AMBIGUOUS. 'sum_t E[KL(q_t||g_t(.|H_t))] <= eps' does not say whether the outer expectation is under P or under P^q. The backward-induction/soft-Bellman derivation implicitly uses the INTERVENED law of H_t (the constraint must be additive along the q-trajectory for a common dual temperature tau to emerge). Under P the problem does not decompose and q* is not the stated Gibbs kernel. The same ambiguity infects KL_tot in T4 and eps in P9, and in combination with error 1 it means the three 'budgets' in the paper are not the same quantity.

NOVELTY CLAIMS FOR T2/T3 NEED A LITERATURE CHECK before they are asserted. For T=1 with binary A and phi an indicator, T2 IS Kennedy (2019) -- the paper says so. Kennedy's incremental-propensity-score paper also treats the time-varying/longitudinal case with an efficient influence function, and there is recent work extending incremental/exponentially-tilted interventions to general and continuous exposures. If so, T2/T3 are a (useful, but incremental) generalization from 'tilt the propensity' to 'tilt along a frozen feature map', not a new demonstration that P-dependent regimes admit multiple robustness. The paper should verify this and say exactly what the delta is; as written the 'runs against the natural expectation' framing overclaims. (Flagged as needs-verification, not asserted as wrong.)

MINOR / PRESENTATIONAL. (a) P8(iii)'s bound 'rho sigma_b sum_t sd(phi_t|H_t)' is a random variable; it needs E[.] or sup_h. (b) P1(iv) and T4(iii) assume phi|H_t conditionally Gaussian, which is incompatible with the finite L of L1 and the bounded phi of A6/A7 -- state it as an approximation. (c) P3(v) 'identified under A9 alone' is true only about OVERLAP; A3 is still doing all the causal work, and the sentence reads as if it were not. (d) Section 1.3 and P3(iii) assert the between-history covariance is negative; this is an empirical conjecture, not a proposition. (e) T5(iii) calls a first-order expansion 'to second order'.
most_important_fix: Repair Theorem T4 and everything downstream of it. The correct identity is E_P[R_T^2] = E_{P^{q^{2theta}}}[prod_t (1 + chi^2_t(H_t))] (equivalently the backward recursion Gamma_t(h) = E[w_t^2 Gamma_{t+1}(H_{t+1}) | H_t = h], Gamma_{T+1} = 1), because w_t^2 = (1 + chi^2_t(H_t)) times the 2theta-tilt weight; the paper's proof implicitly assumes Cov(w_t^2, chi^2_{t+1}(H_{t+1}) | H_t) = 0, which fails whenever tilting moves the conversation into histories with different conditional feature variance. Then (i) drop the claim that the Gaussian case is exact unless sigma_t^2 is history-independent, (ii) re-derive the design rule from Var(D_P) -- the efficiency bound of the estimator actually being recommended -- rather than from the IPW second moment, (iii) fix the measure under which KL_tot is defined and make it the same quantity in T4, T5 and P9, and (iv) redo the numbers with a defensible n_eff^min (with n = 10^4, T = 5, n_eff^min = 100 the budget is about 0.46 nats and 0.96 within-history SD per turn, not 0.9 nats and 1.36 SD). This matters more than any other fix because the exactly-computable variance budget is the route's flagship contribution and the basis of the pre-registration protocol in Section 13; if the pre-committed KL cap is wrong by a factor of two in the permissive direction, the experiment will be pre-registered to report estimates that are not informative.

This is the single load-bearing observation of the route and it is correct.

Theorem T2/T3 as verified algebra: the EIF is tildeQ_1 - Psi + sum_t R_t(tildeQ_{t+1} - tildeQ_t), the action-level critic Q_t(H_t,A_t) genuinely cancels, and double robustness is EXACT (not first-order) in both directions -- I checked the telescoping, the score calculation, the Z_t/barZ_t multiplicative cancellation, and the T=1 IPSI cross-check, and all four are right.

Lemma L1's distinction between a QUANTITATIVE positivity failure (LLM user, full support, variance catastrophe) and a QUALITATIVE support failure (human user, g_t(a|h) = 0 for essentially all a). Keep the idea; redo the efficiency theory.

Section 13's experimental protocol essentially as written -- fixed-seed token-reproducible replay, version-pinned pre-registered phi, a resettable simulator arm, programmatically verifiable Y, a leakage-neutral arm plus an answer-withheld arm, a negative-control tilt on a causally inert feature, a randomized best-of-K calibration arm, reporting per-turn chi^2/ESS/KL_tot/n_eff alongside every point estimate, and clustering against model-version drift.

most_important_fix: Fix the absolute-continuity foundation, which is currently self-contradictory and is load-bearing for the entire §0 verdict. Proposition 1 correctly insists that the logged density is the *truncated* sampler (temperature + top-p/top-k/min-p + logit bias + grammar mask), but Proposition 4 and all of §4 tacitly assume a full-support softmax. Under truncation b_t has restricted, history-dependent support, so for any target whose mask differs (which is exactly the "tilt the token distribution" family) pi is NOT absolutely continuous w.r.t. b and the value is *unidentified*, not merely unestimable. Add an explicit assumption A6' (support compatibility: supp(pi_t(.|h)) subset of supp(b_t(.|h)) at every b-reachable h, verified from the recorded masks), restate Theorem 3 as scoped to support-compatible targets, restate §4's "positivity is vacuous, only a.c. is needed" as "uniform overlap is violated; a.c. holds only under A6'", and redo Proposition 17 accordingly (cross-model reweighting fails a.c. outright, not just variance). This has a clean payoff: the choke-point design of Theorem 6(b) satisfies A6' by construction (targets only reweight fixed generators), which turns the fix into an argument for the design the paper already recommends, whereas token-level tilting is excluded at the identification stage rather than at the variance stage.
errors: Proposition 4 display is false for a stochastic receiver: E_b[W_{1:T}^2] = prod_t 1/b_t(abar_t | h_t) treats h_t as fixed, but h_t contains the random receiver outputs O_1..O_{t-1}. The correct statement is E_b[W^2] = E_b[prod_t b_t(abar_t | H_t)^{-1}], and n_eff = n / E_b[prod_t 1/b_t] <= n E_b[prod_t b_t] by Jensen. The same slip appears in §0 item 1 ('n * prod_t b_t(abar_t|h_t)'). The proof's appeal to 'multiply over turns via Theorem 5(a)' is exactly where the expectation is dropped, since 5(a) leaves the chi-square factor inside E_b[.].

Theorem 6(c)'s proof is wrong. Under a trajectory-level mixture of *stochastic* text-generating policies, A_t is not 'a deterministic function of (J, H_t)' and there IS variation in A_t at fixed H_t, so within-arm sequential ignorability and hence blip identification do hold. The real obstruction is a weight, not an identification, failure: prefix ratios W_{1:t} = dP^{pi(j)}_{H_{t+1}}/dP^{b}_{H_{t+1}} are bounded by m, but a policy that deviates at a *single* turn s has one-turn ratio pi^{(j)}_s/b_s <= 1/P(J=s-arm | H_s), which is unbounded because the arm posterior concentrates once the first message is observed. So Theorem 11's single-turn design cannot be run inside design 6(a). The conclusion survives; the stated proof does not.

Theorem 10(b) drops the dominant variance term. The rollout estimate of Qhat_t(H_t, A_t) enters the DR sum multiplied by W_{1:t}, not W_{1:t-1}. In a language action space you cannot build Vhat_t(h) = sum_a pi_t(a|h) Qhat_t(h,a) from the same rollouts (the sum over a is infeasible), so two distinct noise sources are present: Vhat_t noise weighted by W_{1:t-1} and Qhat_t noise weighted by W_{1:t}. The stated Var ~= sum_t E[W_{1:t-1}^2] sigma_t^2 / m_t omits the larger term. The Cauchy-Schwarz allocation rule in (c) has the right form and the optimal value (sum_t sqrt(alpha_t c_t))^2 / B is correct, but alpha_t is understated.

Proposition 13(b)'s exact randomization test is not exact under an adaptive design. If e_t depends on H_t (and H_t contains O_{t-1}, which A_{t-1} caused), then re-drawing selectors changes the realized histories and therefore changes the assignment densities themselves; the sharp null on Y alone does not make the test statistic recomputable. Exactness requires either a non-adaptive design (e_t depending only on t and past selectors, as in Bojinov-Shephard 2019 temporal experiments) or a sharp null on the entire output path O_1..O_T, which is untenable here. As written the claim of 'exact finite-sample p-values' for a history-adaptive micro-randomized design is false.

Proposition 13(a)'s falsification claim is backwards in the regime where it matters. When E_b[W^2] = exp(D_2) is large, the sample mean Wbar has relative standard error ~ sqrt(E[W^2]/n) and is below 1 with high probability even when every logged density is exactly correct -- this is the standard self-normalization pathology, not evidence of a tokenizer/template bug. The diagnostic has power only when E[W^2] << n, i.e. only in designs whose weights are already bounded. It should be stated as a test conditional on a pre-verified E[W^2]/n budget, and run on bounded prefix weights W_{1:t} for small t.

Internal inconsistency on support (see also the most_important_fix): Proposition 1 makes the truncated sampler the object of interest, while Proposition 4 and §4 assume a full-support softmax. Under top-p/top-k/grammar masking, pi << b fails generically and identification -- not just sqrt(n)-estimability -- is lost. §0's 'no pointwise positivity is needed either, only absolute continuity' is therefore not free, and the paper's own Proposition 2 undercuts its §4 framing.

Proposition 17 understates the failure. With any truncated receiver sampler, M' << M fails outright on the masked tokens, so 'what if we had used model M'' is *unidentified*, not merely variance-punished; the tokenizer point makes it worse but is not the first obstruction. The proposition also omits the (true, but needed) premise that the user mechanism is exogenous and unchanged, which is what licenses reweighting only the receiver factors.

Proposition 16's moment condition is wrong. For the doubly-weighted U-statistic, the kernel's second moment is E[(W_i(pi) W_j(pi'))^2] = E[W(pi)^2] E[W(pi')^2] by independence of the pair, so second moments of each weight suffice for a Hajek-projection CLT; E[W^4] < infinity is not required (it would be relevant only for certain variance-estimator guarantees). Separately, theta(pi,pi') = P(Y^pi > Y^pi') ignores ties, and under a lexicographic hierarchy on (correctness, cost, turns) ties occur with positive probability (identical cost and turn counts), so theta(pi,pi') + theta(pi',pi) != 1; use the net-benefit / win-ratio form with (1/2)P(=) or specify strict tie-breaking, otherwise the 'tournament' in the same paragraph is ill-defined.

Proposition 7's strictness condition is too strong. Variance reduction fails iff rho^sel = rho^mar a.s., i.e. iff tilde-e_{K_t}/e_{K_t} is a.s. measurable w.r.t. (H_t, A_t) -- not iff K_t itself is recoverable. Two selectors with equal ratio tilde-e_k/e_k need not be distinguishable for the bound to be tight.

Theorem 11's n_eff >= n*delta omits the turn-selection factor. The recommended design chooses one turn uniformly at random per conversation, so the effective sample for a *fixed* turn-s blip is ~ n*delta/T, not n*delta (consistent with the §9 'n/6' figure only if all conversations randomize at the same turn). Also, 'the estimand is exactly the blip gamma_s' is imprecise: the displayed quantity is the P^b-average of the blip against the b-continuation, not the conditional function gamma_s(H_s, a, a_ref) the project asks for; recovering the conditional object needs a working model plus g-estimation, which is the content of 11(d).

Theorem 9's telescoping is asserted rather than proved for a policy-chosen random horizon. With tau determined by a STOP action the upper limit of the sum is itself random and action-measurable; the identity requires Vhat_{t+1}(H_{t+1}) := Y on {A_t = STOP} and Qhat_t defined on the STOP-augmented action set, neither of which is stated. Claim (iv) also needs E_b[W^2 Qhat^2] < infinity and cross-fitting: 'no rate condition' is correct for bias, but asymptotic normality with a valid variance still needs Qhat to converge to *some* fixed limit, and boundedness of Qhat.

The assumptions A1-A11 are cited throughout (A1-A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A10, A11) but never stated anywhere in the document, and A9 is never cited at all. Every theorem's 'which assumptions it uses' claim is therefore unverifiable as written, which violates the stated style requirement.

Wording/logic slip in §4: 'Positivity is not violated; it is vacuous.' Uniform positivity b_t(a|h) >= delta > 0 IS violated -- no fixed delta bounds the conditional probability of a message over a growing action set. What is not violated (under full support) is absolute continuity. The intended and correct point is the identification / sqrt(n)-estimability separation under weak overlap; state it that way and cite it (Khan-Tamer 2010; Ma-Wang 2020; D'Amour et al. 2021).

Novelty/citation problems, against the paper's own style rule. (i) The Renyi-divergence ESS reformulation of positivity is Metelli et al. (2018) and, for the second-moment/ESS analysis, Cortes-Mansour-Mohri (2010); calling it 'the most important conceptual contribution available to a Route C paper' overclaims. (ii) 'The statistical estimability constraint D_2 <= epsilon and the PPO-style KL trust region are the *same object*' is false as stated -- different divergences (order 2 vs 1) and, in PPO, typically the reverse direction plus a per-token ratio clip; they are related by monotonicity of Renyi divergences, not identical. (iii) 'no pointwise positivity, only absolute continuity' is the standard condition in the stochastic-intervention/LMTP literature and should be cited as such rather than flagged as 'the first substantive point'.

Theorem 12(d) is loose in a way that undercuts the paper's own case. Since E[min(W,M)^2] <= M E[W] = M, empirical Bernstein gives n >~ M log(|Pi|/alpha)/gap^2, not M^2 log(|Pi|/alpha)/gap^2. This matters: at M = m (Theorem 6a) the corrected rate is exactly the cost of a plain stratified A/B test over the m arms, whereas the stated M^2 rate makes the OPE machinery look a factor m *worse* than the design it replaces -- gratuitously strengthening the objection already conceded in §10.4.

Numerical inconsistency in the horizon argument. §0 item 2 and §5 assert T is 3-10 and that the multiplicative-in-T curse is 'mild', justified with T = 4. But at T = 10 and delta = 1/6, delta^{-T} = 6^10 ~ 6e7, which is not survivable at any realistic n. Either restrict the claim to T <= 4-5 or state the delta-T frontier explicitly.

Proposition 2 mislabels a discarded chain-of-thought as 'a mediator'. It sits on the H_t -> A_t path, i.e. it is pre-treatment latent generation randomness, not a mediator of the A_t -> Y effect. Ignorability is indeed unharmed, but for that reason (it is not a common cause of A_t and Y outside H_t), not the stated one.

Proposition 15 needs one more assumption to be true. Identifying the value of a *suggestion* policy by reweighting e_t requires the user's response kernel P(A_t | H_t, S_t) to be invariant to the suggestion policy. If users adapt to the suggestion mechanism (learning it, anchoring, or reacting to its perceived quality), the ITT estimand is not identified by reweighting alone. State this as an explicit invariance/no-feedback assumption rather than leaving the ITT claim unconditional.

Section 10 as a whole, especially 10.4 (the four legitimate reasons for OPE when you could just run the target policy) and 10.1 (identified but never estimable). This is the standard of candor the rest of the project should be held to.

errors: Thm 2, off-by-one in the indicator. The display has 1{T>tau}; the correct event is 1{T>=tau} (equivalently 1{R_t=1 for all t<tau}, i.e. N>=tau-1), because the turn-tau factor 1{R_tau=0}/b^R_tau(0|H_tau) marginalizes to 1 given that psi(H_tau) is H_tau-measurable, which is exactly what the proof says. As written the estimand drops all units that stopped exactly at tau, is biased downward by E[W psi(H_tau) 1{T=tau}], and no longer has E[W 1{...}]=1 (so the ESS identity n/E[W^2] in Prop 16, which needs E[W]=1, is also off). The paper's own sanity check at tau=2 uses 1{R_1=1}=1{T>=2} and thus contradicts the displayed formula.

Prop 3 (prophet sandwich): the restriction 'tau<=T' is either near-vacuous or the inequality is false. If tau<=T a.s. and tau is adapted, then at every history where pi continues we must have b^R_t(1|H_t)=1, so the admissible class contains only rules that never override -- in realistic logs essentially tau<=2. If instead the sup ranges over implementable rules that can force continuation, the inequality fails. Counterexample: b^R_1(1|X)=0.01, psi(H_1)=0, psi(H_2)=1 on continuation. Then V(tau==2)=E[1{R_1=1}psi(H_2)/0.01]=1, while E[max_{t<=T} psi(H_t)]=0.01. So the advertised reporting device ('at most X is recoverable by ANY stopping rule') is not licensed. Fix: state it for the truncated regime tau'=min(tau,T); E[psi(H_{min(tau,T)})] IS an unweighted observed mean under A7, so the sandwich becomes correct AND genuinely weight-free -- and incidentally shows a whole class of early-stopping estimands needs no weights at all, which strengthens the route.

Prop 11(b), scalar case: the claim that the extreme couplings are comonotone/antimonotone and that the bounds are 'Frechet-Hoeffding-type' (Makarov/Ruschendorf) is wrong. c(v,w)=1{v>w} is neither supermodular nor submodular (check v=0,v'=2 against w=-1,w'=1 versus w=1,w'=3: the two submodularity inequalities go in opposite directions), so monotone rearrangements are not extremal. With identical continuous marginals the comonotone coupling gives P(V>W)=0, the countermonotone coupling gives 1/2, but sup over couplings is 1 (approached by rank shifting). Makarov/Ruschendorf bounds are for the law of a difference, not for P(V>W). The qualitative conclusion ('generally wide') survives; the characterization does not.

Prop 8(iii) is false as stated. 'With eta_1>0 the optimal rule stops in the interior' requires that the per-turn probability of an out-of-tolerance improvement eventually falls below the top-priority tie probability. If that probability is bounded away from zero for all t<=K_bar (e.g. constant 0.5), the lexicographic optimum is still K_bar even with eta_1>0. The proof text itself smuggles in the missing hypothesis ('once the per-turn probability ... falls below the tie probability'), which is not part of the assumption set.

Thm 12(ii) is proved only for flat truth. The displayed inequality sup_tau E[Yhat_tau] - sup_tau E[Y*_tau] >= (optimal-stopping value of noise) is asserted in general but the proof begins 'take Y* constant'. It is also filtration-ambiguous: if the second sup is over rules adapted to the true path (an oracle) rather than to the observable filtration, the difference can in principle be negative because the noisy observer loses information. State it either for flat truth or with both sups over the same observable filtration, and note the result is the pure-noise lower bound only in the former case.

Prop 16's last claim mis-identifies the probability limit under a positivity violation. Where b^R_t(1|H_t)=0, the IPW estimator gives those trajectories weight zero, so it converges to the support-restricted functional in which off-support trajectories are credited 0 (or, self-normalized, to the support-conditional value) -- NOT to 'the value of the regime that stops whenever the natural user would', which would credit psi(H_{min(tau,T)}). The distinction matters because the actual failure mode is a downward bias of known sign, not a silent substitution of a sensible truncated regime.

Prop 14(a) is internally inconsistent with the stopping-only framing. If pi intervenes on R_t, then acceptance is pi's own decision, so lambda^acc cannot simultaneously appear as a natural cause-specific hazard inside E^pi; under A4/A10 the only stochastic termination left is abandonment. Separately, the display double-counts survival: if E^pi is an expectation over trajectories generated under pi, the continuation/termination events are already realized in the measure, so multiplying by prod_{s<t}(1-lambda^acc_s-lambda^ab_s) is wrong. The formula needs to be written as an explicit g-formula integral over covariate transitions with the intervened termination mechanism substituted.

A14 / Thm 9: a tolerance rule is a semiorder, not a total preorder, so the utility representation does not exist. 'Ties when the difference is within eta_1' gives an intransitive indifference relation (y ~ y+eta ~ y+2eta but y < y+2eta), hence there is no u with Psi(z,z')=sign(u(z)-u(z')). The proof silently replaces the tolerance by a fixed binning, which is a different (and boundary-dependent) estimand: two values differing by less than eta_1 across a bin edge are scored as a win. Constructive repair that is strictly more general: for ANY bounded pairwise comparison Psi and a fixed reference pi_0, define f(z)=E[Psi(z, Z^{pi_0})]; then theta_NB(pi,pi_0)=E[f(Z^pi)] with f in [-1,1], no representability needed, and Thm 9(i)-(iii), Thm 6 and Thm 7 go through verbatim. The mid-rank transform is then just the special case Psi=sign(u-u').

OPEN #3 is misdiagnosed. With prespecified Psi (or u, eta), theta is bilinear in (F_pi, F_{pi_0}) and therefore pathwise differentiable with bounded derivative -- no smoothness is required, as Thm 10's own derivation shows. The actual problem with data-adaptive u or eta is not loss of differentiability but a data-dependent estimand (the target changes with the sample), which calls for prespecification for a different reason.

Prop 13 and its executive-summary gloss. (a) gamma_hat = gamma* - beta holds only if the continuation arm adds exactly one turn; in general gamma_hat = gamma* - beta E[N_cont - N_stop | H_t], so the bias is larger and history-dependent. (b) 'if beta >= lambda the estimated optimal rule never stops before K_bar' additionally needs free disposal (true marginal gain >= 0); with quality degradation it can still stop. (c) The summary's 'biases the estimated optimal stopping time late by beta/lambda in cost units' does not follow and is dimensionally incoherent: Prop 13 delivers a threshold shift of beta in quality units; converting a threshold shift into a shift in stopping TIME requires the slope of the marginal-gain profile in t.

Thm 6(i) overclaims 'the stop arm needs no outcome model' and A6 is correspondingly too weak. The claim is true only under an unstated measurement assumption: Y must be post-hoc computable on every prefix (programmatic outcome, or the judge re-run on the frozen prefix artifact). If Y is realized only at the actual termination (user-reported, session-valued, or judged once at the end), then Q_t(H_t,STOP)=E[Y | stop at H_t] is a causal contrast requiring STOP-arm positivity, so A6 must be two-sided: delta <= b^R_t(1|H_t) <= 1-delta. Also, as literally written, 'it is E[psi(H_t)|H_t]' is vacuous, since psi(H_t) is H_t-measurable by definition; the intended object is E[judge score | H_t] with judge noise -- exactly the channel Thm 12 then indicts.

Prop 1 / A10 versus the recommended micro-randomized design. The cancellation of b^L is exact for the estimand 'set R_t=1, then draw the message from b^L(.|H_t,R_t=1)', but that conditional law is estimated from VOLUNTARY continuers, and no experiment can realize a draw from it: a nudged/forced user writes a different message. In an MRT the randomized object is a nudge Z_t, not R_t, so identification of gamma_t requires (i) an exclusion restriction (Z_t affects Y only through R_t) and (ii) invariance of the message mechanism to the nudge. If (ii) fails, the numerator's text density is the nudged one, the b^L factors do not cancel, and Prop 1 fails -- i.e. the route's headline advantage evaporates and one is back in Route B territory. Section 6.3 flags ITT-vs-per-protocol but never notes this consequence for Prop 1.

gamma_t is overloaded with two different functions. Thm 6 defines gamma_t = Q(STOP) - Q(CONTINUE then pi) and then uses the optimal continuation in the Bellman recursion, whereas Thm 7 defines gamma_t under the NATURAL continuation policy b. The sign rule 'STOP iff gamma_t >= 0' is optimal only for the pi*-version; the exact performance-difference decomposition holds only for the b-version. They coincide only at the last turn. The two must be given distinct symbols, and the design corollary (which claims one blip function determines every stopping regime) is true for the b-version only.

Cost is dropped without notice. V(pi) is defined as E[Y^pi - lambda C^pi], but Thm 2, Prop 3 and Thm 7 display pure quality functionals. Either say explicitly that psi absorbs -lambda C_{tau-1} (legitimate, since accrued cost is H_tau-measurable) or carry the cost term; as written Thm 2's 'V(pi)=' is a different object from the definition in Section 1.

Prophet-inequality constants are transferred outside their hypotheses. Krengel-Sucheston's factor 2 requires independence and Correa et al.'s 0.745 requires i.i.d. draws from a KNOWN distribution with a single selection. The quality path psi(H_t) is a dependent, unknown, history-driven process, so 'prophet inequalities bound how much of the gap an online rule can capture' is not licensed here (it is licensed inside Thm 12(ii), where the sequence really is i.i.d. noise).

Prop 4 is stated for exact zeros, but the operative regime is b^R_t(1|H_t) approximately 0, where point identification technically holds and the sharp-bound statement does not apply. The honest object is a delta-trimmed estimand (Crump et al. / Petersen et al. style) with the trimming mass reported, plus the finite-sample near-violation story; kappa_0 as defined is measure-zero in most realistic models. Also the 'cost of the forced turns is known' step is not exact when the number of forced turns after hitting the null set is itself path-dependent.

Thm 10's rate conditions are incomplete. Two nuisance functionals of the potential-outcome laws are plugged in (G_0^- and Gbar_pi), but only G_0 is cross-fitted in the stated conditions; Gbar_pi is itself an estimated potential-outcome functional and its error must be shown to enter at second order, and the product-bias condition should be stated per arm (||bhat^R - b^R|| times ||Qhat - Q|| = o(n^{-1/2}) for each of pi and pi_0), not once.
most_important_fix: Re-found the route on an implementable continuation arm, and fix the two identification statements that depend on it. Concretely: (1) Replace A10's 'leave the text at its natural law' with a DECLARED message mechanism. The b^L cancellation in Prop 1 is mathematically exact but its estimand requires realizing a draw from b^L(.|H_t, R_t=1) -- the conditional message law of voluntary continuers -- which no experiment can implement, because a nudged user writes a different message and a randomized nudge is an instrument, not the treatment. So state the identified target as an LMTP with an explicit generator G (G = a fixed prompt-template library, a candidate generator LLM, or the nudge's own ITT effect), add the exclusion restriction 'nudge affects Y only through R_t' and the invariance condition 'nudge does not shift the message law', and admit that if the latter fails the language density does NOT cancel and Prop 1 fails. (2) In the same pass, correct Thm 2's indicator to 1{T >= tau} (all R_t = 1 for t < tau) -- the current 1{T > tau} drops the units that stopped exactly at tau, biases V(pi) downward, breaks E[W]=1 and contradicts the paper's own tau=2 check -- and restate Prop 3 for the truncated rule tau' = min(tau, T), for which E[psi(H_{min(tau,T)})] really is an unweighted observed mean under A7. That restatement both repairs the false 'upper bound for any stopping rule' claim and yields the route's strongest genuinely new result: a large class of advisory early-stopping regimes ('stop when the rule says, or when the user quits, whichever comes first') is identified with NO weights, NO positivity and NO exchangeability -- which is a cleaner headline than the current one and is immediately experimentally actionable.
keep_these_ideas: The action factorization A_t = (R_t, tilde A_t) with intervention on the binary coordinate only, so that positivity is required on a two-point set while the language density cancels from the likelihood ratio. This is the right structural move and is the route's real contribution.

The reframing of 'the curse of horizon' as a curse of OVERRIDE DEPTH d rather than of conversation length T (Thm 2(ii), Prop 16): log W is the natural-user surprisal of the regime's own continuation path, so delta^{-d} with d in {1,2} replaces delta^{-T}. This is correct, quantitative, and immediately usable for design.

The structural non-identification argument of Prop 4: continuation probability is decreasing in current quality, so the positivity failure sits exactly on the histories where 'would one more turn have helped?' is interesting. This is a design verdict, not a nuisance, and it is the most valuable honest statement in the document.

Thm 12 (winner's curse of optimized stopping) and Prop 13 (horizon-correlated judge bias): the observation that in Route E the measurement nuisance direction IS the treatment coordinate, so the best-documented LLM-judge pathologies map one-to-one onto estimand bias. The recommendation of two prespecified independent measurement channels (one for stopping, one for scoring) plus a horizon-invariance calibration test (score the same frozen artifact presented as a 1-turn and a 5-turn conversation) should survive into any version of the paper.

Prop 15's dichotomy: truncation by death is a property of the OUTCOME DEFINITION (artifact-valued vs session-valued), not of the endogenous horizon, and is therefore designed away rather than bounded. The corresponding instruction to avoid satisfaction/acceptance as the primary outcome is correct and non-obvious to this field.

The interface-isolation version of separable effects (Prop 14d): decomposing the turn-t action into what is rendered into the receiver's context versus what reaches only the user's continuation decision, with isolation guaranteed by inspecting the rendered prompt -- a software guarantee rather than a statistical assumption. This is the most transportable idea in the route.

The reduction of a prioritized/win-ratio terminal outcome to a bounded pseudo-outcome against a FIXED reference, so that backward induction and the whole scalar DTR apparatus apply unchanged, together with the honest statement that the resulting optimum is reference-dependent because pairwise win probabilities need not be transitive. (Use f(z) = E[Psi(z, Z^{pi_0})] rather than the mid-rank/utility construction.)

Section 7's category-error warning: because N and C are chosen by the regime, reporting 'our regime causes fewer turns' as an estimated effect is incoherent; N and C belong inside the value, not on the left-hand side of an effect estimate.

The requirement that an implementable stopping rule be a stopping time with respect to decision-time observable signals, with anything reading an end-of-episode oracle score labelled explicitly as a prophet benchmark.
The 'shared budget pool as an interference channel specific to Route E' observation (one trajectory's length consumes another's available horizon), with per-task budget pools as the fix.

The reporting discipline of publishing kappa(pi) (extrapolation mass) and the distribution of log W as headline diagnostics alongside every evaluated regime, with bounds rather than point estimates wherever kappa > 0.

The leakage score proposal: run the receiver on the candidate message alone with no history and score the result, then either hold that score fixed by a fixed template library or stratify on it and report its distribution by arm.
